comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: Proven possible headlessly during the seam work: load target/debug/libmuster.dylib, dispatch Startup + AttachPane, spawn muster-bridge at the returned socket path, dispatch KeyDown, then read the pane back with herdr's pane.read. `echo hi` echoed. Worth writing as a Rust integration test against muster-seam rather than in Python - the probe used to prove it hand-rolled protobuf, which would rot.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Retitled: this said 'contract tier' because the default gate was not allowed a daemon. It is now, so this moves into the ordinary suite rather than a tier beside it.

The shape is unchanged and the recipe from the previous comment still holds - attach, spawn the bridge at the returned socket, send keys, read the pane back - but it is a Rust integration test spawning the pinned daemon, not a Python script run out of band. The daemon harness it needs is the same one the mirror's connection tests need, so they should be built together and it should not land before that harness exists.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: The daemon harness this needed now exists: crates/herdr-harness, built for the mirror's ten daemon-backed tests. One daemon per test, killed on drop, isolated by pointing XDG at a scratch root. What is left here is the input-path half - a program in the pane, encoded keys sent, the grid snapshotted - which is the oracle this card always described.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Done. crates/muster-bridge/tests/input_path.rs runs in the ordinary
gate: a real daemon from herdr-harness, a real muster-bridge process,
`cat -v` in the pane, and the screen as libghostty-vt computes it.

Both routes are covered, which needed one trick worth remembering. In a
pane's default mode the local encoder and the daemon both turn Up into
ESC [ A, so an arrow test there passes whether or not the server route
worked at all. The pane is put into application cursor mode first: the
right answer becomes ESC O A while Muster's blind profile still says
ESC [ A, so a fallback is visible. Verified by forcing the fallback -
the test failed with ^[[A on screen.

It lives beside the bridge rather than beside the seam because cargo
hands CARGO_BIN_EXE_<name> only to the owning package's tests, and one
test per binary because the seam's attached pane is a process global.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
The input path is verified end to end today by a throwaway script: isolated daemon, cat -v in a pane, muster-bridge relaying, assert the bytes that arrive. That check is worth keeping and is not in the suite, because the default tier must stay offline and deterministic (docs/testing.md).

Shape: the contract tier docs/testing.md already describes - real version-pinned herdr, isolated config dir, throwaway session per test, synchronized by event waits rather than sleeps. The oracle is the grid harness that already exists: put a program in the pane, send encoded keys, snapshot what the screen becomes.

Worth doing once there is a second thing to verify this way, so the tier is built for two cases rather than shaped around one.
title: Run the input path against a real herdr, in the gate
